image_prompt.text: The central stone castle keep with battlements and a pitched tower roof, tall enough to be seen from anywhere in the fortification so players always know where the middle is
Cobblestone routes threading the courtyard from the main gate to the keep and around the houses, giving the ground an obvious grain to walk along
Composed views of the keep framed by the gate archway and the line of the battlements, built to look right from the courtyard floor
The defensive stone curtain wall closing the courtyard, with trees and foliage massed around the perimeter beyond it so the map edge is hidden behind the fortification's own defences
The main gate, a wide stone archway through the curtain wall, composed so the keep is the first thing players see on the way in
A few smaller houses inside the courtyard, medieval-style with pitched wooden roofs and wooden doors

layout_placement.text: Players arrive at the main gate archway, facing into the courtyard toward the keep

notes: Classified None: the prompt describes a place — a medieval fortification and its geometry — rather than a game type. 'Explore and fight in' is the only gameplay wording and no combat feature is asked for, so no genre was invented. If fighting turns out to be real, Action merges by shared ID with nothing lost.
All five axes left at their defaults: exterior, single-surface, single zone, dressed, grounded-surface. Routes P0.

Prompt asks for configurable attributes for wall height, building count, and overall scale. No option carries parameters, and 'a few' houses is not a stated count, so no count field is emitted and the wording is kept in the text.
Stone-for-walls / wood-for-roofs-and-doors was folded into the option texts rather than carried as a separate pick.

would have asked: Sounds like an explorable place — a central castle keep as the landmark you navigate by, cobbled routes threading the courtyard, and composed views of the walls and tower. I would add the curtain wall as the map edge with the perimeter treeline behind it, the main gate archway as where you arrive, and the houses inside the courtyard. Want that as-is? Judged it a fit and took it.

would have asked: Do players actually go inside the keep or the houses, or are they solid from the outside? Took exterior-only, which keeps this on the proven single-pass build; enterable interiors need a separate indoor pass that is not ready yet, and I would note it for when it is.

would have asked: Do players walk the battlements and the wall-walk, or are they scenery to look at? Built as one ground surface; play on surfaces stacked above the courtyard needs overhanging-surface support, which is not ready yet.
would have asked: The one signature option the preset does not already include is a gathering area — an open space in the courtyard sized for a crowd. Want one?
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
